outlook: Grains were mixed in Wednesday morning trade. November soybeans were up 7½ cents at $12.91¼, staying inside their recent range, after China reported September soybean imports of 11.88 million tonnes, down 7.7% from a year earlier, and the EPA on Tuesday proposed that larger refiners blend more biofuels over the next two years, which could support demand for soybean oil and corn. December corn eased ½ cent to $4.82¼ as the market keeps consolidating after the October WASDE, with mostly dry weather letting harvest speed up and some rain expected in the western Corn Belt later this week. Wheat was lower across all three exchanges, with Minneapolis December spring wheat down 2½ cents at $6.91½, after USDA put winter wheat planting at 51% versus a 58% five-year average and IKAR trimmed Russia's crop to 88.0 million tonnes, in line with USDA; ICE November canola was up C$6.20.
